scope: XSS surfaces, token leakage, untrusted payload trust boundaries
head: d3dc4c2c6

xss_surface_analysis.summary: The wizard uses innerHTML extensively to render its UI. All user-controllable inputs (item names from backend, sauce/extras names from backend, customer instruction text) flow into HTML strings. Risk classification depends on whether the source is trusted (admin-controlled DB) or user-controlled (instruction note).

html_string_injection_sites.context: Voir tous button onclick attribute uses .innerHTML mutation with hiddenCount integer. Source = integer, NOT user-controlled. Safe.
Same pattern for viande Voir tous button.

btn.innerHTML = emoji + ' ' + displayName. emoji comes from VIANDE_EMOJIS/SAUCE_EMOJIS maps (hardcoded constants). displayName comes from backend item.name OR i18n key. Backend name is admin-controlled; treated as trusted per Laravel SaaS convention.
html_string_injection_sites.mitigation_present: Backend admin uses Spatie Permissions ACL; only Admin/Branch Manager can edit item names. No public surface to inject arbitrary names.

html_string_injection_sites.context: headerEl.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', '✅ Complet'). Static string. Safe.
.innerHTML = newHtml in UI update paths. newHtml built locally from controlled selection state + backend item names.

wizardEl.innerHTML = renderSinglePage(). renderSinglePage() returns a large HTML string built by composing per-step render functions (renderViandeStep, renderSauceStep, etc.). Each step inserts item name + emoji + thumbnail URL via string concatenation.
html_string_injection_sites.mitigation_present: All sources are backend-emitted from Laravel resources (NormalItemResource, ItemAttributeResource, ItemExtraResource). Backend does NOT use Blade auto-escaping for ItemAttribute->name in API payloads — it returns raw strings. POS is Admin-only; no public surface. Treated as trusted in current threat model.
html_string_injection_sites.concern: If an attacker compromises an admin account (or there's an account takeover via separate vector), they could inject HTML/JS by setting an item name to ''. This would execute when a POS operator opens the wizard on that item. Real risk = lateral movement post-compromise.

thumbnail_url_injection.logic: If thumb provided, returns ''. No HTML-encoding of thumb URL.
thumbnail_url_injection.risk: If thumb contains double-quote + onload= → XSS. Source = backend NormalItemResource->thumb which is a Spatie Media URL. Generated by Laravel, not user-controllable today.
thumbnail_url_injection.mitigation_present: Spatie Media URLs are deterministic + slugified; no admin input.

comment_textarea_handling.logic: commentTa.addEventListener('input', function () { instructionText = this.value; ... }). The instructionText is then echoed into HTML via .innerHTML in renderRecapStep (search shows it appears in cart_display strings).
comment_textarea_handling.risk: User-typed instruction is the ONLY user-controlled string in the wizard. If echoed via .innerHTML without escaping, this is a self-XSS (only the operator who typed it sees their own output). Cross-user XSS only possible if instruction text is persisted and rendered on KDS / OSS surfaces unescaped.
comment_textarea_handling.search_needed: Whether KDS/OSS Vue components render instruction via {{ }} (auto-escaped) or v-html (vulnerable). Wizard side is internal-only.

token_leak_surfaces.summary: POS Wizard does NOT directly handle tokens. Sanctum kiosk:order tokens belong to Kiosk surface (per CLAUDE.md §9). POS uses session cookies with CSRF middleware.
token_leak_surfaces.csrf_handling: Wizard does NOT send any XHR/fetch itself. It only intercepts incoming responses (read-only XHR/fetch overrides at pos-wizard.js:170-215) and dispatches a synthetic DOM event ('wizard:add-to-cart') that Vue ItemComponent consumes. The actual order POST goes through the existing Vue/axios pipeline with CSRF token already attached.

global_window_state.name: window.POS_WIZARD_CONFIG
global_window_state.source: admin-pos-v4.blade.php:129-135 — server-rendered Blade with Smartisan\Settings prices

global_window_state.name: window.foodkingConfig
global_window_state.contents: baseUrl, apiKey (config('app.api_key')), googleMapKey, demo, kiosk locale + pricing config, posV4Entry flag
global_window_state.risk_assessment: config('app.api_key') is server-rendered into window. This is intentional for POS API calls (acknowledged in audit AUDIT_W2_DEDICATED_ENTRY_CLAUDE_2026-04-26 D.1 — demo creds REMOVED but apiKey kept). Acceptable per POS surface threat model (admin-authenticated only).
global_window_state.concern: If POS surface is ever exposed via a public route or shared screen without auth gate, apiKey leaks. Today: Admin-auth-only via routes/web.php. Safe.

global_window_state.name: window.fetch override + XMLHttpRequest override
global_window_state.risk: These prototypes are globally patched. Any other script on the page could observe the wizard's interceptor as a side effect. POS Blade loads ONLY pos-app.js + pos-wizard.js + theme JS (drawer/modal/dropdown). No third-party scripts. Risk: NONE in current loadout. Backlog: document that POS Blade must never include analytics/3rd-party JS before pos-wizard.js.

dom_attribute_payloads.validation: JSON.parse in try/catch; checks injected.itemAttributes || .variations || .extras presence
dom_attribute_payloads.risk: Vue-controlled, same-origin. Trusted. If Vue's serialization were XSS-tainted, the threat is already at the Vue layer.

dom_attribute_payloads.validation: JSON.parse in try/catch; Object.assign into selections. NO schema validation.
dom_attribute_payloads.risk: An attacker who could inject this attribute could pollute selections with arbitrary keys. But Vue is same-origin and trusted. Real risk = a downstream XSS in Vue letting attacker drive a payload that confuses subsequent submit logic.
dom_attribute_payloads.recommendation: WIZ-REC-4 in architect.json — schema validation for restored selections

dom_attribute_payloads.validation: Wizard writes, Vue reads. Same-trust boundary.

intercepted_xhr_responses.logic: On every XHR load whose URL matches admin/item/*, JSON.parse(responseText), assign to lastItemData if structure matches. Try/catch swallows errors.
intercepted_xhr_responses.risk: If a same-origin endpoint returns malformed JSON, wizard ignores it. If a malicious admin/item/* endpoint were ever introduced returning attacker-controlled JSON, wizard would trust it. Mitigation: same-origin routes auth-gated; not a realistic vector today.

untrusted_payload_trust_boundaries.openssl_csrf_or_xsrf_in_wizard: None — wizard does not initiate network requests

side_effects_global_prototype_patches.rationale: Necessary because Vue's axios uses XMLHttpRequest under the hood and there's no other ergonomic way to observe ItemComponent's response payloads without modifying Vue (frozen).
side_effects_global_prototype_patches.risk: Global prototype patching is a maintenance hazard but not a security one in this context. No third-party JS on POS Blade.

blade_view: fonts.googleapis.com + fonts.gstatic.com via preconnect (admin-pos-v4.blade.php:25-27) — first-party-controlled URLs
Local CSS: fonts (themes/default/fonts/*), pos-wizard.css, mix('css/app.css'), custom.css
Local JS: mix('js/manifest.js'), mix('js/vendor.js'), mix('js/pos-app.js'), theme JS (drawer/modal/customScript/tabs/dropdown), pos-wizard.js with ?v={time()} cache-bust
Analytics sections rendered via {!! $section->data !!} (admin-pos-v4.blade.php:47, 60, 75) — UNESCAPED admin-controlled HTML insertion. CRITICAL trust boundary.

analytics_unescaped_render.context: {!! $section->data !!} renders raw admin-saved HTML into HEAD/BODY/FOOTER. This is Laravel-standard for analytics tags (GA, GTM), but it's a high-trust surface. Admin can inject arbitrary JS via the Analytics admin page.
analytics_unescaped_render.mitigation_required: Admin-auth-only + permission:settings gate on Analytics CRUD routes. If those are correctly gated, risk is acceptable for an internal SaaS tool. PS-1 audit cannot verify routes — defer to broader admin route audit.

medium_summary: MED-1: .innerHTML rendering of admin-controlled item names creates lateral-movement XSS post-admin-compromise. Acceptable risk in admin-only POS surface; backlog WIZ-SEC-1: escape item names in renderSinglePage paths or migrate to DOM-builder.
MED-2: Customer instruction text echoed via .innerHTML. Self-XSS only at POS surface, but check KDS/OSS Vue templates use {{ }} not v-html. Backlog WIZ-SEC-2: cross-surface instruction render audit.
verdict.summary: Wizard security posture is acceptable for the current admin-only POS threat model. No critical issues. Two MEDIUMs are lateral-movement risks worth tracking as V1.0.X backlog. The analytics {!! !!} unescaped render in the Blade view is by-design admin trust; orthogonal to wizard.
